polaris: For amorphous In2O3 and related transparent conducting oxides without long-range periodicity, is band-like transport sufficiently diagnosed by Anderson/Mott mobility-edge filling, or by a medium-range metal-s-orbital connectivity network plus O-O/coordination-defect thresholds?
framework: Network science / weighted percolation. Treat a-In2O3 as a 3D effective In-s hopping graph, not as a blurred crystal band that automatically survives disorder.
findings: The nonstandard criterion is graph percolation of the In-s conduction network. Proposition B becomes sharp if giant component fraction, effective degree, edge/corner-sharing connectivity, and O-O defect edge-killing predict spectral ridge collapse, IPR growth, level-statistics drift, Drude-weight loss, and Hall mobility loss better than EF-Ec at matched carrier density.
math_object: Weighted graph G=(V,E,w). V are In sites. E are In-In pairs capable of effective In-s hopping. w_ij = exp(-(r_ij-r0)/lambda) * S_ij * D_ij, where S_ij encodes corner/edge sharing and D_ij penalizes O-O or coordination defects. The deeper object is the spectrum of the weighted adjacency/Laplacian and the Anderson Hamiltonian defined on this graph.

graph_abstraction.nodes: One node per In atom. Node attributes: In-O coordination, local polyhedral distortion, distance to nearest O-O defect.
graph_abstraction.edges: Connect In_i and In_j when r_ij < r_cut and an O bridge or spatial overlap supports effective In-s hopping. Edge attributes: r_ij, corner-sharing flag, edge-sharing flag, shared-O count, local O-O defect penalty.
graph_abstraction.weights: t_ij = t0 * exp(-(r_ij-r0)/lambda) * (1 + alpha_edge*I_edge + alpha_corner*I_corner) * exp(-beta*f_OO_local). Fit from Wannier/QSGW if available; otherwise use this as a geometry proxy.
graph_abstraction.transport_mapping: Build H_ij = epsilon_i*delta_ij + t_ij; compute IPR, adjacent-gap ratio, spectral-ridge proxy, and Drude/Kubo proxy; compare with Hall mobility at fixed carrier-density bins.

one_to_two_week_metrics.definition: S_GC = N_largest_connected_component / N_In, computed for both unweighted and t_ij > t_min thresholded weighted graphs.
one_to_two_week_metrics.expected_use: B predicts nonlinear mobility/ridge/Drude collapse when S_GC crosses a sample-family threshold.
Use as a percolation control variable. The threshold should be calibrated from the structural ensemble rather than assumed universal.

one_to_two_week_metrics.definition: P(r_In-In), medium-range peak areas, and edge density inside r_cut.
one_to_two_week_metrics.expected_use: Separates samples with similar carrier density but different In-s overlap topology.

one_to_two_week_metrics.definition: f_OO = N(O-O distances below defect cutoff or peroxo-like motifs) / N_O; also compute local f_OO around each edge.
one_to_two_week_metrics.expected_use: Models O-O defects as edge deletion or edge weakening, not merely onsite disorder.

one_to_two_week_metrics.definition: R_edge = N_edge-sharing/(N_edge-sharing+N_corner-sharing); R_corner analogously; also record per-node sharing-type degree.
one_to_two_week_metrics.expected_use: Distinguishes a merely dense graph from a truly 3D In-O-In connected hopping backbone.

falsifiable_predictions.statement: At matched carrier density, S_GC or z_eff crossing a threshold predicts Hall mobility and Drude-weight collapse better than EF-Ec.
falsifiable_predictions.observable: mu_H, Drude weight D, S_GC, z_eff, f_OO
falsifiable_predictions.test: Across melt-quench, annealing, or oxygen-defect ensembles, compare cross-validated models mu_H ~ S_GC+z_eff+f_OO versus mu_H ~ EF-Ec after binning by carrier density.
falsifiable_predictions.expected_direction: mu_H and D fall nonlinearly when S_GC<S_c or z_eff<z_c; similar EF-Ec does not rescue high mobility if network connectivity is below threshold.

falsifiable_predictions.statement: Spectral ridge broadening, IPR increase, and level-statistics Poissonization synchronize with the network threshold.
falsifiable_predictions.observable: A(k,E) ridge linewidth Gamma_k, IPR(EF), adjacent gap ratio r_bar
falsifiable_predictions.test: In a graph Hamiltonian or DFT/Wannier supercell, progressively delete or weaken low-quality defect edges and track S_GC, Gamma_k, IPR, and r_bar.
falsifiable_predictions.expected_direction: Near the same network window, Gamma_k rises, IPR(EF) rises, and r_bar shifts from Wigner-Dyson-like toward Poisson-like statistics.

falsifiable_predictions.statement: O-O defects behave as network edge killers; equal-amplitude onsite disorder that does not damage In-s connectivity should be less destructive.
falsifiable_predictions.test: Compare two perturbations: onsite-only disorder versus O-O-position-guided edge weakening/deletion at matched energy variance.
falsifiable_predictions.expected_direction: Edge-killing disorder destroys ridge coherence and extended states faster than onsite-only disorder.

strangest_prediction: A sample can have EF nominally above a fitted mobility edge and carrier density comparable to a good conductor, yet lose effective band ridge, Drude-like response, and Hall mobility together if its In-s graph falls below the weighted percolation threshold.

deepening_1.question: Does the isomorphism have a deeper mathematical layer?
deepening_1.answer: Yes. Ordinary percolation asks only whether a giant component exists. The deeper layer is a graph-spectral transition: weighted-adjacency spectral radius rho(A_w), Laplacian algebraic connectivity lambda_2, and the Anderson-Hamiltonian mobility edge may be three projections of the same connectivity transition. In this view, mobility edge is not denied; it is reinterpreted as the spectral shadow of the In-s weighted graph.

deepening_2.question: Does the borrowed network idea have a next-level extension in its home field?
deepening_2.answer: Yes. Ecological and traffic networks analyze robustness under targeted attack, betweenness bottlenecks, and multiplex layers. Mapping back: O-O/coordination defects may preferentially kill high-betweenness bridge edges rather than random edges; edge-sharing and corner-sharing are two multiplex hopping layers. A graph with many total edges but damaged bridge edges should collapse earlier than a randomly diluted graph.

a_objection: A will object that network metrics are just renamed disorder strength and can be absorbed into Ec. B's answer: if matched-n and matched-EF-Ec samples differ strongly in S_GC/z_eff/f_OO and spectral/transport collapse follows the network threshold, then A becomes a post-hoc fit rather than a sufficient criterion.
failed_jumps: Traffic shortest-path congestion was rejected as the main framework because electron states are coherent quantum states rather than classical packets.
Ecological trophic cascade was kept only as a robustness analogy because trophic hierarchy has no clean mapping to In-s hopping energy hierarchy.
next_plan: Round 2 should implement a minimal structure-to-graph script: input amorphous In2O3 coordinates, output S_GC, z_bar, z_eff, P(r_In-In), f_OO, and edge/corner ratio; then build a tight-binding graph Hamiltonian and scan t_min or f_OO to compute IPR, r_bar, spectral proxy, and Drude proxy.
